title: Best Sportsbook for Professionals (2026)
verdict: For a professional bettor in 2026 the best sportsbook is the venue that solves the operational problem, not just the pricing problem: one account, every venue, best price, size filled, and no limits for winning. That is TerminalUp. It routes orders across nineteen live venues, sportsbooks, exchanges and prediction markets, and never takes the other side.

The professional's reference book is still Pinnacle, and the US book that behaves like one is Circa. This page treats them as what they are: excellent single venues that are better used through a terminal than on their own.

ranking.lacks: A $10,000 minimum and no proprietary lines.
ranking.note: One account across Pinnacle, Betfair, Matchbook, Novig, ProphetX, SX Bet, Kalshi, Polymarket, predict.fun and more. Best fee-adjusted price and size per outcome, cross-venue fills, a published Odds API with sandbox keys. 0.5% commission per trade, 0.35% at the highest volume, no subscription.

why: The hidden cost of professional betting is operations: a dozen accounts, balances stranded where you got limited, three KYC queues, and a spreadsheet to remember which book still takes you. TerminalUp collapses that. You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it. Nineteen venues are live as of November 2026, sixteen more are in the pipeline, and none of them needs its own login.

The board is built for size. Each outcome shows the best fee-adjusted price across every connected venue, the size available at it, and the ladder beneath. The order ticket routes to the best venue and fills across several when one is thin. For desks running models, the TerminalUp Odds API delivers the same cross-venue prices over REST, Server-Sent Events and WebSocket.

Commission is 0.5% per trade, 0.35% at the highest volume, no subscription and no deposit fees. TerminalUp never holds a position, so it has no reason to limit a professional, which is the one thing every sportsbook eventually does.
